newsitem.title: RUSSIA: IFC mulls Gazprom inclusion in composite index.
newsitem.headline: IFC mulls Gazprom inclusion in composite index.

text.p: The International Finance Corporation (IFC) may exclude natural gas monopoly Gazprom from its investable indices because of restrictions on foreign trading of the instrument, the IFC said on Wednesday.

But fourteen other shares in the IFC's leading Russian index will be included in a composite index tracked by major funds, probably on November 1, IFC head market analyst for central and eastern Europe Constantinos Grigoriadis said in a statement.

"Since Gazprom is not open to foreign investment (I mean to buy locally) we have to decide either to take it out of the IFCI (IFC Investable) Russia when the index will join the IFCI Composite or to change the IFC index methodology to include ADR (American Depositary Receipt) prices," he said from Washington.
"No decision yet," he added. The Russia investable index, launched in February, tracks major companies in which shares may be readily bought.

The IFC has a number of indices tracking emerging markets and about $7-8 billion tracks the chief index, the IFC investable, Grigoriadis said. Russia's addition to the lead index will mean new fund allocations to the Russian market.

Gazprom has restrictions on foreign ownership of its shares. It has an ADR, which allows foreign trading of the shares, priced at a steep premium to locally-traded shares, and has said repeatedly it would defend the two-tier share structure.
Gazprom shares on the Russian Trading System closed at $0.64 on Tuesday and Gazprom ADRs, which cover 10 underlying shares each, closed at $15.125 in London.

The other fourteen shares in the Russia IFCI which will be included in the composite index are the following: LUKoil Holding, Surgutneftegaz, UES, Mosenergo, Rostelekom, Noyabrskneftegaz, Irkutskenergo, Yuganskneftgaz, Megionneftegaz, St Petersburg Telephone, Purneftegaz, Norilsk Nickel, Chernogorneft and KamAZ.
